tracks.narration: Computers only store ones and zeros — so where does the minus sign come from? Two's complement is the trick.
To negate a number, flip every bit, then add one. Take three: zero zero one one. Flipped: one one zero zero. Plus one: one one zero one — that is minus three.

Sweep through every 4 bit pattern from minus eight to plus seven. The most significant bit acts like a sign — zero on the positives, one on the negatives — and the value wraps cleanly around at minus eight.
The pay off — addition just works. Five plus minus three: line up the bits, ripple the carries, and you land on two with no special case for the sign.
Flip and add one — that one rule lets a computer subtract using only the same adder it uses to add.
